sims.title: Components, and why the resultant is not the sum
sims.intro: Move the sliders. The dashed lines are the components of A — signed numbers, not vectors — and the red arrow is the resultant you would get by adding components separately, which is the only method that works.
watch: Aₓ goes negative the moment A passes 90°, while |A| never does. That is the whole difference between a component and a magnitude.
Set both directions equal: only then does |R| equal A + B. Every other angle gives less, which is why magnitudes cannot be added.
Make the two antiparallel and watch |R| fall to |A − B| — the smallest resultant two vectors can have.

challenges.prompt: Set A's direction so that its x-component is zero while its magnitude stays 5.
challenges.explain: At 90° the vector points straight up the y-axis: cos 90° = 0, so Aₓ = 0 and Aᵧ = A. A component can vanish while the vector itself is as long as ever.

challenges.prompt: Point B at 217° and read |R|. Then check the direction the calculator would have given you from arctan alone.
challenges.explain: With both resultant components negative the true direction is in the third quadrant, but arctan(Rᵧ/Rₓ) reports an angle in the first. Adding 180° is the fix, and the picture is what tells you to.
